title: Understanding Debt-to-Income Ratio (DTI)
content: Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio is a personal finance measure that compares an individual's total monthly debt payments to their gross monthly income. It is expressed as a percentage: (Total Monthly Debt Obligations / Gross Monthly Income) * 100. Lenders use DTI to assess borrowing capacity and credit risk. A lower DTI ratio indicates a healthy balance between debt and income, while a high DTI (above 40-50%) indicates potential over-leverage and financial strain.
